newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed seeks bigger say for Russia with NATO.
newsitem.headline: Lebed seeks bigger say for Russia with NATO.

text.p: Security chief Alexander Lebed said on Saturday Russia should deepen cooperation with NATO and work out an agreement to ensure its voice is heard by the Western alliance, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Lebed, who visited NATO headquarters in Brussels this week, complained that Russia had played a "passive" role in the alliance's Partnership for Peace (PFP) scheme designed to step up cooperation with former foes in central and eastern Europe.

"This participation (in PFP) must be permanent, systematic. Russia must work out what it wants, what it is for and against," Tass quoted Lebed as saying at Russian strategic missile troops' central command in Odintsovo, southwest of Moscow.
Russia has made little effort to move ahead with projects planned under PFP, a scheme which NATO countries regard as a way to build trust and forge a better relationship with Moscow.

Lebed said Russia should have a permanant representation at NATO headquarters and reach an agreement based on three principles which he defined as: "We take decisions together, carry them out together and take responsibility together."
It was not clear what kind of agreement Lebed was demanding and whether it would cover the whole range of Moscow's relations with NATO or just certain issues.
The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation has rejected demands by Russia to have a right to veto decisions such as which countries can become members.
Lebed accepted Russia had no right to a veto during his visit to Brussels, despite his opposition to NATO expanding to include Moscow's former Warsaw Pact allies.

NATO officials lauded Lebed for his moderate language during his visit to Brussels. But the gruff former paratroop commander, who has set his sights on becoming president, again criticised NATO's expansion plans on Thursday after returning to Moscow.
